title: Gasoline Safety (consumer fact sheet: refuelling, filling containers, storage, disposal; guidance from the American Petroleum Institute)
licence_note: State government fact sheet reproducing American Petroleum Institute consumer guidance; archived for personal offline reference. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: place a portable container on the ground and keep the nozzle in contact with it while filling; never fill a container inside a vehicle, trunk, pickup bed, flat bed or trailer floor; fill slowly; do not get back into the vehicle while refuelling; never siphon by mouth, and if gasoline is swallowed do not induce vomiting; fill no more than 95 percent full; gasoline vapours are heavier than air and can travel along the floor to an ignition source; store away from water heaters, space heaters and furnaces; never pour old gasoline on the ground or into a drain.

title: Fire Hazard from Filling Portable Gas Cans in Pickup Trucks and Cars (Hazard ID, July 1998)
org: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH); copy hosted by eLCOSH (CPWR)
licence_note: US federal government work (NIOSH). Read 2026-11-16 by R3: fires occurred when portable gasoline containers were filled in pickup beds (plastic bed liners) and cars; remove containers from the vehicle and place them on the ground before filling; touch the container with the nozzle before removing the lid; keep the nozzle in contact with the container inlet while filling.

title: Stop Static Campaign (three rules for safe refuelling)
licence_note: PEI grants permission to use the information unaltered and not for profit, with acknowledgment. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: static electricity can ignite gasoline vapours at the pump; almost 200 incidents reported to PEI; rules: turn off the engine, do not smoke, never re-enter the vehicle while refuelling.

title: Gas Engineering Guide: LP-Gas Tank, Vapor LPG Tanks (Note A, DOT cylinders, quoting NFPA 58 6.3.7)
licence_note: Gas utility engineering guide; archived for personal offline reference. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: for DOT cylinders, the pressure relief device is at least 3 ft horizontally from any building opening below the level of discharge, and at least 5 ft horizontally from any exterior source of ignition, openings into direct-vent appliances, or mechanical ventilation air intakes (NFPA 58 6.3.7).

title: LP gas inside buildings (fire code information sheet)
org: Minnesota Department of Public Safety, State Fire Marshal Division
licence_note: State fire marshal guidance; archived for personal offline reference. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: cylinders larger than 1 pound must not be stored or used indoors at a residential property, including attached and detached garages; maximum container size in residential occupancies is 1 lb.

title: 49 CFR 173.6, Materials of trade exceptions (regulation text)
org: US Department of Transportation, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (Code of Federal Regulations)
licence_note: US federal regulation. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: Packing Group II or III materials in packagings of not over 30 kg (66 lb) or 30 L (8 gallons); packagings leak tight for liquids, securely closed, secured against shifting and protected against damage; aggregate gross weight of all materials of trade on a motor vehicle not over 200 kg (440 lb).

licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: flash point -45 F; lower explosive limit 1.4 percent.

title: Methanol: Systemic Agent (Emergency Response Safety and Health Database)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: swallowed methanol can cause metabolic acidosis, blindness and death; breathing high vapour concentrations is as effective as swallowing in producing toxic effects; the odour does not warn of low exposures.

title: Homeowner Resources and FAQs (how often to sweep; chemical cleaners; glazed creosote)
licence_note: © CSIA; archived for personal offline reference. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: quotes NFPA 211, 'Chimneys, fireplaces, and vents shall be inspected at least once a year for soundness, freedom from deposits, and correct clearances'; masonry fireplaces should be swept at 1/8 inch of sooty buildup, sooner if any glaze is present; hard or tacky glazed creosote cannot be removed by normal brushing and needs a professional's chemical treatment.

title: Wind Chill Chart (chart graphic with frostbite times, effective 11/01/01)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: wind chill formula and table by temperature and wind; frostbite-time shading of 30, 10 and 5 minutes. At 10-25 mph the 30-minute band begins at about -19 to -24 F wind chill, the 10-minute band at about -37 F (25 mph) to -47 F (10 mph), the 5-minute band at about -64 F (25 mph) to -71 F (15 mph).

title: During a Heat Wave
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: wear lightweight, loose-fitting, light-coloured clothing; sunburn reduces the body's ability to get rid of heat; use fans to exhaust hot air or draw in cooler air; do not direct a fan at yourself when the room is hotter than 90 F; infants and young children are particularly vulnerable; never leave children in a car.

title: Understanding Heat Alerts (Extreme Heat Warning, Extreme Heat Watch, Heat Advisory)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: an Extreme Heat Warning is issued when extremely dangerous heat is expected or occurring; a Heat Advisory for dangerous heat below warning criteria; avoid outdoor activity in the heat of the day, drink plenty of water, rest in shade.

title: Logging operations, 29 CFR 1910.266 (personal protective equipment, paragraph (d)(1))
licence_note: US federal regulation. Read 2026-11-16 by R3: chain-saw operators wear cut-resistant leg protection covering the thigh to the top of the boot, and cut-resistant foot protection; head protection where objects can fall or fly; eye and face protection; hand protection against cuts and punctures.
